titel: 261. what if part of you doesn’t want to get better? (feat. dr. blaise aguirre)

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen: keine Merkmale gefunden, aber eine unveraenderte Wiederholungsprobe beweist nichts

einzeiler: Dr. Blaise Aguirre discusses teen mental health, self-hatred, and finding agency in DBT.
kurzfassung: Host Sadie Sutton sits down with Dr. Blaise Aguirre to discuss her time in residential treatment at McLean Hospital eight years ago. They explore why personal agency and curiosity are critical for effective mental health treatment compared to power struggles. Additionally, they examine the nature of self-hatred as an identity and the hidden costs of using self-criticism to drive high achievement.
stichpunkte: Dr. Blaise Aguirre returns to the podcast to discuss mental health evolution and treatment insights six years after his first appearance.
Sadie reflects on her intake at McLean Hospital's 3East program at age 14, where Dr. Aguirre asked if she actually wanted to be there.
Effective mental health treatment requires personal agency, autonomy, and aligning goals with what the individual genuinely wants for their life.
Parents often fall into counterproductive power struggles and threats instead of practicing curiosity and validation with struggling teens.
Mental health struggles like anxiety, OCD, and depression heavily interplay as comorbidities rather than existing in isolation.
Severe emotional pain and psychological suffering are real and logical based on biology and genetics, despite not being physically visible.
Deeply ingrained self-hatred can function as a core identity rather than a temporary state, making it feel like a constant companion.
High-achieving individuals often use negative self-evaluation to fuel success, but it frequently comes with a heavy hidden cost to their relationships and well-being.

kapitel.titel: The Importance of Agency and Intake
The Hidden Costs of High-Achieving Self-Criticism

clips.hook: Do you want to be here?
clips.text: Dr. Blaise Aguirre opened their initial meeting by asking whether the patient actually wanted to be present, emphasizing that recovery requires personal agency rather than passive treatment.

clips.hook: No two brains are the same
clips.text: Over the past eight years, the focus has expanded to address how multiple psychological conditions overlap rather than treating a single primary diagnosis in isolation.

clips.hook: When you get into a battle with your child, you've already lost
clips.text: Instead of increasing punishments or ultimatums, caregivers achieve better results by showing curiosity and validating the struggling person's perspective.

clips.hook: How can a bright person have asthma?
clips.text: Mental health struggles affect intelligent individuals just as physical illnesses like asthma do, proving that cognitive ability does not prevent psychological conditions.
Dialectical behavior therapy helps teenagers reclaim autonomy by reframing harmful coping habits as past survival tactics and evaluating their ongoing costs.

beschreibung:
why are some people afraid to ask for help, even when their mental health is getting WORSE?! today’s guest is dr. blaise aguirre—an assistant professor in psychiatry at harvard medical school in the department of psychiatry. he is a child and adolescent psychiatrist and the founding medical director of the 3east dialectical behavior therapy continuum of care at harvard affiliated mclean hospital.

in this episode, i’m reuniting with dr. aguirre to discuss how my treatment at 3east saved my life– and why this program worked for me when nothing else did. dr. aguirre also draws his clinical expertise to unpack all things teen mental health, breaking down topics including self-hatred, agency, family dynamics, & more!

whether you’re struggling with your mental health or love someone who is, this episode is your guide to what makes treatment actually work.

we talk about:
03:27 what makes teenagers more likely to accept help for their depression

12:52 why mental health challenges aren’t an intelligence issue
17:13 the role of self-hatred in depression
20:38 how depression can impact our relationships
23:40 what really motivates us to change our worst habits
